name: Stephen
bio: Stephen, full of faith and the Holy Spirit, was one of seven men chosen by the disciples to oversee the daily distribution of food, freeing the apostles to focus on prayer and teaching; the apostles prayed and laid hands on him and the other six. Full of faith and power, Stephen performed great wonders among the people. When members of a synagogue disputed with him but could not out-argue his Spirit-given wisdom, they incited false witnesses to accuse him of blasphemy against Moses and God before the council, claiming he said Jesus would destroy the temple and change the law of Moses; those watching him saw that his face seemed like the face of an angel (Acts 6:1-15). His trial, defense, and martyrdom are told in detail in the chapter ahead. Before the council, Stephen recounted Israel's history from Abraham through Moses and the wilderness tabernacle to Solomon's temple, rebuking his accusers as stiff-necked people who, like their ancestors, resisted the Holy Spirit and had now betrayed and murdered the Righteous One. Enraged, the council dragged him out of the city; as he was stoned, Stephen saw a vision of heaven opened and Jesus standing at God's right hand, prayed for the Lord to receive his spirit and to forgive his killers, and died — the first Christian martyr. The witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul (Acts 7:1-60).
